name: Museu do Fado (Fado Museum)
seoTitle: Fado Museum: An Hour of Lisbon Song, 6 Minutes from Port
tagline: A compact museum of Lisbon's own music, six minutes' flat walk from the ship

description.short: A small, well-organised museum on the history of fado, Lisbon's urban song, with recordings, Portuguese guitars and portraits of the great fadistas. It sits at the bottom of Alfama, about 400 m from the cruise terminal.
description.full:
The Fado Museum is the easiest cultural visit of any Lisbon port day. It stands on Largo do Chafariz de Dentro at the foot of Alfama, about 400 m and a flat six-minute walk from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal, so it works as the first stop after you step ashore, the last stop before all-aboard, or a dry hour if it rains.

The permanent exhibition follows fado from the 19th-century taverns of Alfama and Mouraria to the international stage. The part most visitors remember is the listening: recordings of singers from different decades let you hear how the style changed, and the wall of portraits of fadistas gives faces to the voices. There is also a section on the Portuguese guitar, the 12-string, pear-shaped instrument that gives fado its sound. An audioguide is available in English, French and Spanish as well as Portuguese.

Most people need 60 to 90 minutes. If you are short of time, go straight to the listening points and the guitar section; 45 minutes is enough for the essentials.

The museum is closed on Mondays, so check your call day before planning around it. Tuesday to Sunday it opens at 10:00, which is usually quieter than late morning, when walking groups heading into Alfama pass through the square. Admission is 5 euros for adults and free for children up to 12 and for Lisboa Card holders.

The museum pairs naturally with a walk up through Alfama: the Miradouro de Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol viewpoints are a steep 15 minutes above it, and on Tuesdays and Saturdays the Feira da Ladra flea market runs at Campo de Santa Clara, a short uphill walk away. If your ship stays overnight, visiting the museum first gives useful context for an evening fado house in the same neighbourhood.
description.history: The museum opened in 1998 in the former Recinto da Praia water pumping station, an industrial building on the square where Alfama's residents once collected water from the Chafariz de Dentro fountain. The location is fitting: fado grew up in these streets in the first half of the 19th century, sung in taverns and sailors' bars before it moved into theatres, radio and records in the 20th century. Amália Rodrigues took it worldwide from the 1950s. In 2011 UNESCO inscribed fado on its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, in a candidacy prepared by the city of Lisbon with the museum.
description.significance: It is the one place in Lisbon where fado is explained rather than just performed. For a visitor with only a few hours, it turns a style of music you may hear in passing into something you understand: who the key singers were, why the guitar sounds as it does, and how the songs relate to the city around you. Its location makes that possible without any transport.

directions.general: Located in lower Alfama near the Tagus River waterfront, between Santa Apolónia train station and Terreiro do Paço
directions.fromCruisePort: About 400 m and 6 minutes on foot from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal, on Largo do Chafariz de Dentro at the bottom of Alfama; flat all the way.
directions.publicTransport: Metro to Santa Apolónia station (Blue Line), then 10-minute walk. Buses 735, 759, 794 to nearby stops. Tram 28E stops in Alfama but requires uphill walk. From Terreiro do Paço, 15-minute walk through lower Alfama.
directions.parking: Limited street parking. Nearest parking at Santa Apolónia station. Not recommended to drive - narrow streets. Walk or use public transport.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open Tuesday to Sunday; closed Mondays

admissionPrices.notes: Adult 5 euros. Ages 13 to 25: 2.50 euros. Seniors 65+: 4 euros. Children up to 12 free. Free for adult Lisboa Card holders. Tickets can be bought online or at the desk.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Opening time (10:00) or mid-afternoon on Tuesday to Sunday. The museum is closed on Mondays.
busyPeriods: Late morning, when walking tours pass through Alfama
June, during the Santo António festivities in Alfama
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Allow 60 to 90 minutes. Use the audioguide and prioritise the listening points. Closed on Mondays and on 1 January, 1 May and 24, 25 and 31 December. Last admission 17:30.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 1.5 to 2 hours including the walk (6 minutes each way)
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Flat 400 m walk from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal. The museum states it has wheelchair access and lends two manual wheelchairs free of charge.
tips: Closed on Mondays and on 1 January, 1 May and 24, 25 and 31 December: check your call date first.
Adult tickets are 5 euros; children up to 12 are free, and visitors aged 13 to 25 pay 2.50 euros.
Lisboa Card holders enter free, which makes it a good first stop if you have bought the card for transport.
Last admission is 17:30, so it also works as a final stop before an evening all-aboard.
With under an hour, head straight for the listening points and the guitar section.
Pick up the audioguide at the desk; the recordings are the core of the visit.
From here, the climb to the Santa Luzia viewpoint takes about 15 minutes on steep streets and steps.
Tram 28 does not stop outside; walking up through Alfama is quicker than queuing for it.

highlights: Listening points with recordings of fadistas across the decades
Portrait wall of fado singers and musicians
Material on Amália Rodrigues and other leading performers
Former 19th-century pumping station building on Largo do Chafariz de Dentro
Temporary exhibitions and occasional events (check the museum's agenda)
facilities: Audioguide in Portuguese, English, French and Spanish
Children's audioguide in the same four languages
Museum shop with fado recordings and books
Two manual wheelchairs available on free loan

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Fully wheelchair accessible with elevator and ramps. Accessible restrooms available. Wheelchair-height exhibits and listening stations. Seating available throughout museum. Assistance available - call ahead if needed.
